title: Internal Forecasts in Multi-Location Firms

scopes.description: All three supplied code branches: the main Census SAS-to-panel R program, the separate R1A prepared-CSV/MOPS R program, and the Stata IBES analyst-forecast appendix program. Cross-branch outputs are not inferred.

requirements.description: Prepared annual sales analyst-forecast detail input read by the Stata appendix as Analyst_Forecast_2018_Full.dta. The author query selects annual sales forecasts with FPI 1, 2, 3 and 4; the supplied code further filters MEASURE == SAL, keeps FPEDATS from June 30, 2017 through May 31, 2018, and requires announcements at least 20 months before period end. The code also consumes ACTUAL from this forecast-detail input.

routes.description: Readable local I/B/E/S Detail History with Actuals candidate. The full frozen native schema and one-row complete-field probe include every field the supplied code consumes, including ACTUAL, plus FPI for the author-documented query. The authors specify annual sales forecasts (FPI 1–4), and the code applies MEASURE == SAL, 2017 forecast period ends and a 20-month announcement cutoff using these exact fields. This provides a complete compatible source route for staging the prepared DTA input; original author bytes are not needed.
routes.expected_period: Author query selects FPI 1–4; supplied code filters MEASURE == SAL, FPEDATS from June 30, 2017 through May 31, 2018, and announcements at least 20 months before period end.

routes.description: Readable unadjusted I/B/E/S Detail History candidate with the author query fields, but its complete frozen native schema and bounded probe omit ACTUAL, which the supplied program directly consumes from Analyst_Forecast_2018_Full.dta. The separate actuals file is later used to construct SALES_2015 and SALES_2017; no source-supported separate join constructs the detail ACTUAL field before the code’s comparison. This unadjusted candidate therefore does not supply the complete forecast input contract; it is not a data-access finding.
routes.expected_period: Author query selects FPI 1–4; supplied code filters MEASURE == SAL and forecast period ends in 2017.

routes.description: The packaged sample file probe reports only CUSIP, not the fields consumed by the Stata forecast detail branch. It is not used by the supplied code and is not a substitute route.

requirements.description: Separate prepared annual sales actuals input read as Actuals_2015_2017.dta. The supplied code selects MEASURE == SAL, CURR_ACT == USD, and fiscal-year windows for FY2015 and FY2017, aggregates VALUE by TICKER, then merges SALES_2015 and SALES_2017 into the forecast sample.

routes.description: Readable local I/B/E/S Actuals File candidate with exact-case required columns in the full frozen schema and one-row probe. The authors document an annual sales actuals query; the code applies MEASURE == SAL, CURR_ACT == USD, the FY2015/FY2017 PENDS windows, aggregates VALUE by TICKER and merges those results into the forecast sample. This provides a complete compatible source route for staging the prepared DTA actuals input; the code’s ±0.01 comparison is a later alignment check.
routes.expected_period: Fiscal years 2015 and 2017; PENDS windows are filtered in the supplied code, with USD and SAL filters.

issues.description: The Census-based R branches depend on application-controlled confidential business microdata. The datasheet describes application access for approved researchers, while current authorization and exact working roots are unknown. Raw SAS/CSV field vectors and some path roots are redacted, so native field and full history contracts cannot be completed from the supplied material. This is not a finding that the data or a permitted route is absent.

The R1A branch consumes five prepared CSVs under a redacted local.directory, but the package does not contain those files or a source-supported producer/handoff from the main R entry point. The raw field mappings are redacted. Their exact source paths, columns and transformations remain unresolved.

Three executable programs are supplied, but no master program or documented cross-entry handoff links their outputs. Main R reads restricted SAS inputs, R1A reads separate prepared CSVs plus its own SAS MOPS read, and Stata reads two prepared IBES files. Keep these branches separate unless the author supplies a combined order; the supplied evidence does not support deriving the R1A CSVs from main R.

R1A executes reads of lbd2015.csv and forecasts/asm2015mops.csv at the start, but lbd2015 is not used later and the mops2015 CSV object is overwritten by a SAS read before its first use. Without a proposed deletion, the current script still attempts to open both files. The two reads can be removed without changing downstream computation based on the source trace.

evidence.description: Stata source reads the prepared forecast file, documents the IBES Detail History query and FPI 1–4 selection, and applies fiscal-year and announcement-date rules using the exact raw fields.
evidence.quote:
use  "Analyst_Forecast_2018_Full.dta"
//this file is generated by querying IBES details file on WRDS for annual sales forecasts  (FPI 1, 2, 3, 4)
gen year_FPE = year(FPEDATS)
gen month_FPE = mofd(FPEDATS)
gen monthFPE = month(FPEDATS)
//classify FPE between June 30, 2017 and May 31, 2018 as 2017 FY
keep if month_FPE >= 689  & month_FPE <=700
//want forecasts made at least 20 months before FPE
gen FPE_20 = month_FPE - 20
gen month_ANNDATS = mofd(ANNDATS)
keep if month_ANNDATS <= FPE_20
//keep most recent forecast for each analyst
gsort TICKER FPEDATS MEASURE ANALYS -ANNDATS
by TICKER FPEDATS MEASURE ANALYS: gen nvals = _n == 1
keep if nvals
//stale forecasts
gen month_REVDATS = mofd(REVDATS)
gen diff = FPE_20 - month_REVDATS

evidence.description: Stata source reads the separate prepared IBES actuals file.

evidence.description: Stata source filters actuals by fiscal-year window, USD currency, sales measure and nonmissing values.
evidence.quote:
gen year_PENDS = year(PENDS)
gen month_PENDS = mofd(PENDS)
//2015 FY ends between June 30 2015 and May 31 2016
//2017 FY ends between June 30 2017 and May 31 2018
gen FYEAR = 0
replace FYEAR = 2015 if month_PENDS >= 665 & month_PENDS<=676
replace FYEAR = 2017 if month_PENDS >=689 & month_PENDS<=700
keep if FYEAR == 2015 | FYEAR == 2017
//drop non USD
drop if CURR_ACT != "USD"
keep if MEASURE == "SAL"
drop if missing(VALUE)

evidence.description: Stata source writes ACTUAL_to_merge.dta from actuals and later reads it keyed by TICKER.

use Analyst_Forecast_Clean_2018
keep if MEASURE == "SAL"
drop if  VALUE <=0
merge m:1 TICKER using "ACTUAL_to_merge.dta"

evidence.description: Main R maps panel input columns to named survey, identifier, geography and production targets.
evidence.quote:
setnames(panel.long, asm.cols[2:15], 
         c('SURVU_ID',"FIRMID","inTABULATION","YEAR",'statecode',"MSA",'zipplus4','stateabbr', 'TotValShip','InterPltXfer','TotEmp','TotCapEx', "numberProd","NAICS"))
panel.long[,YEAR := as.integer(ifelse(is.na(YEAR),2017,YEAR))]
panel.long <- panel.long[inTABULATION=='Y'&lbdnum_vintage21!=""]
setorder(panel.long, lbdnum_vintage21,YEAR,SURVU_ID,-TotValShip)
panel.long[,ZIP := ifelse(nchar(zipplus4)==9,substr(zipplus4,1,5),ifelse(nchar(zipplus4)==5,zipplus4, ""))]

####### Some entries have multiple SURVU_IDs for a LBD number in a given year, combine for the values that make sense.  
# Sum numeric values
panel.asm <- dcast(panel.long[inTABULATION=='Y'&lbdnum_vintage21!=""],lbdnum_vintage21~YEAR,fun.aggregate = function(x){if(length(x)==0) NA else sum(x)},
                   value.var = c("TotCapEx","TotEmp", "TotValShip","InterPltXfer","numberProd"))
# Pick first for FIRMID and NAICS
panel.header <- dcast(panel.long[inTABULATION=='Y'&lbdnum_vintage21!=""],lbdnum_vintage21~YEAR,value.var = c("FIRMID","NAICS"),fun.aggregate = function(x){x[1]})
# Infer the Geographic location from the most recent entry with a zipcode, otherwise the most recent entry
geog.loc <- panel.long[,.(lbdnum_vintage21,YEAR,TotValShip,ZIP,stateabbr,MSA,statecode)]
setorder(geog.loc,lbdnum_vintage21,ZIP,-YEAR,stateabbr,MSA,statecode,na.last=TRUE)
geog.loc <- geog.loc[,.SD[1],by=lbdnum_vintage21]
geog.loc$TotValShip  <- NULL
geog.loc$YEAR <- NULL

panel <- merge(geog.loc, panel.header, by="lbdnum_vintage21")
panel <- merge(panel, panel.asm, by="lbdnum_vintage21")
